theorem_title: Theorem 1.1 — no Borel bound modulo null sets at $\Delta^0_3$
formal_statement:
theorem ModNullUniversality.theorem1_1 :
    ∃ K : ModNullUniversality.CompactMetrizableHaarGroup,
      ModNullUniversality.IsAbelian K ∧
      ∃ H : ModNullUniversality.WF → Subgroup K.Carrier,
        ModNullUniversality.LowComplexityFamily K H ∧
        ∀ F : ModNullUniversality.StandardBorelEquivalence,
          ∃ T : ModNullUniversality.WF,
            ∀ C : Set K.Carrier, MeasurableSet C → K.haar C = 1 →
              ¬ ModNullUniversality.BorelReducible
                (fun x y : C => ModNullUniversality.CosetRelation K (H T) x.val y.val)
                F.rel := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
There are one compact metrizable abelian group $K$, its normalized Haar probability $\lambda$, and one family of subgroups $(H_T)_{T\in\mathrm{WF}}$ with the following properties. Every $H_T$ is $\Delta^0_3$ in $K$. Every graph $\{(x,y):x^{-1}y\in H_T\}$ is $\Delta^0_3$ in $K^2$ and is a difference of two $F_\sigma$ sets. For every Borel equivalence relation $F$ on an arbitrary standard Borel space there is a well-founded tree $T$ such that

$$E_{H_T}^K\mathbin{\upharpoonright}C\not\leq_B F
\qquad\text{for every Borel }C\subseteq K\text{ with }\lambda(C)=1.$$

The compact group, measure, and whole family precede the arbitrary target. The selected tree may depend on $F$, but it must work against every Borel conull domain for that target. No invariance of $C$ is required. A reduction on $C$ would have to preserve and reflect the relations on every pair in $C^2$, not just almost every pair for the product measure. Empty target spaces are included; no countability of the full well-founded-tree index set is imposed.

There exist a type \(G\), a group structure on \(G\), a compact metrizable topology on \(G\) for which multiplication and inversion are continuous, a measurable-space structure on \(G\) equal to the Borel \(\sigma\)-algebra of that topology, and a measure \(\mu\) on this measurable space such that \(\mu(G)=1\), \(\mu\) is invariant under left multiplication by every element of \(G\), every compact subset has measure strictly less than \(+\infty\), and every nonempty open subset has strictly positive measure; these choices satisfy \(xy=yx\) for every \(x,y\in G\), and there exists a function \(T\mapsto H_T\) assigning a subgroup of \(G\) to every \(T\) in the following indexing set \(\mathcal W\): an element of \(\mathcal W\) is a Boolean-valued function on all finite lists of natural numbers such that, for every finite list \(s\) and every natural number \(k\), the value true on \(s\) followed by \(k\) implies the value true on \(s\), and there does not exist a function \(b:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\) for which \(T([b(0),\ldots,b(n-1)])\) is true for every \(n\in\mathbb N\), including \(n=0\), where the list is empty; there is no requirement that the empty list have value true, so the function that is false on every list is included in \(\mathcal W\), as is the function true only on the empty list. Each \(H_T\) is a subset of \(G\) containing the group identity and closed under multiplication and inversion, and the function assigning these subgroups is subject to the following conjunction of conditions, with no additional regularity in its argument \(T\) specified: for every \(T\in\mathcal W\), both the subset \(H_T\) of \(G\) and the subset \(R_T=\{(x,y)\in G\times G:x^{-1}y\in H_T\}\) of \(G\times G\) have each of the following two representations in their respective ambient topology (the product topology for \(R_T\)): there exists a sequence \((U_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\) of subsets with the given subset equal to \(\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}U_n\), where for every \(n\) there exists a countable collection \(\mathcal O_n\) of open subsets of the ambient space such that \(U_n=\bigcap_{O\in\mathcal O_n}O\); and there exists a sequence \((V_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\) of subsets with the given subset equal to \(\bigcap_{n\in\mathbb N}V_n\), where for every \(n\) there exists a sequence \((D_{n,m})_{m\in\mathbb N}\) of closed subsets of the ambient space such that \(V_n=\bigcup_{m\in\mathbb N}D_{n,m}\). In addition, for every \(T\in\mathcal W\) there exist subsets \(A,B\subseteq G\times G\) and sequences \((A_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\), \((B_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\) of closed subsets of \(G\times G\) such that \(A=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}A_n\), \(B=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}B_n\), and \(R_T=A\setminus B\). All natural-number indices in these conditions start at zero; the countable collections of open sets may be empty, whose intersection is the whole ambient space, and the sets occurring in these representations may themselves be empty or the whole ambient space. Finally, for every choice of a type \(Y\), a measurable-space structure on \(Y\) for which there exists a Polish topology (a topology induced by a complete separable metric) having precisely that Borel \(\sigma\)-algebra, and a relation \(F\) on \(Y\) that is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive and whose graph \(\{(u,v)\in Y\times Y:F(u,v)\}\) is measurable for the product measurable-space structure, there exists \(T\in\mathcal W\) such that, for every subset \(C\subseteq G\), if \(C\) is measurable in the specified Borel \(\sigma\)-algebra on \(G\) and \(\mu(C)=1\), then there does not exist a function \(f:C\to Y\) that is measurable with respect to the measurable-space structure on the subtype \(C\) induced by its inclusion in \(G\) and the specified measurable-space structure on \(Y\), and that satisfies \(x^{-1}y\in H_T\) if and only if \(F(f(x),f(y))\) for every \(x,y\in C\), with \(x,y\) regarded as elements of \(G\) in the group expression. This is an existential assertion about the choices of \(G\), its structures, \(\mu\), and the entire subgroup assignment; the choice of \(T\) in the final condition may depend on the specified measurable space \(Y\) and relation \(F\), but must work for every such \(C\). Empty target spaces \(Y\) are included, with the equivalence-relation conditions then vacuous and with no function from a measure-one \(C\) to such a target; the group \(G\) and each measure-one \(C\) are nonempty, \(C=G\) always satisfies the two hypotheses on \(C\), and subsets \(C\) failing either hypothesis impose no condition.
